openings.claim: Extra left-corner compression may be unnecessary for lateral retention: removable edge-registering clips could carry sideways load through hatch-edge and rim contact while retaining the existing seal and centered hatch.
openings.delta: Remove the hypothesized dependency on tightening the left corner. Shape supplied strips into removable rim clips with padded contacts and M4 adjustment; use their shoulders as lateral stops. Cord keeps detached clips recoverable outside the inspection opening.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: friction from stronger corner compression is necessary. Registration predicts displacement at most 1 mm under 20 N without extra left pressure, whereas tighter-left retention may reproduce opposite-corner lift. Success under the right-contact card would counterexample the compression dependency; failure does not establish its necessity or any converse.
openings.probe: First check whether rim access, strip shaping with supplied tools, and adjustable clip geometry permit capture without hatch/rim deformation. If feasible, conduct ten candidate opening/closure/pull trials, the tenth disturbed; record position, 20 N displacement, reopening time and visible seal condition. Use two ordinary tighter-left reference trials, one disturbed: twelve total, two configurations. Reference trials compare immediate behavior only. Stop upon visible tearing or permanent deformation; stopping alone provides no successful test.
assumptions: Rim underside access and hatch-edge geometry accommodate positive stops; neither is supplied.
Supplied strips can be shaped and adjusted within ninety minutes using the stated tools.
Four clips can be cleared, with their cord, within thirty seconds by one technician.

Defeat conditions: inaccessible rim, strip yielding or escape at 20 N, more than 1 mm displacement, corner lift that prevents secure closure, seal tears, obstructing tethers, or excessive removal time.

assessment: This is an untested removal hypothesis, not deployment. Positive registration offers a possible counterexample to necessary extra corner pressure, but indispensable geometry and fabrication capacity remain unknown. All outcome requirements and constraints remain binding, including the disturbed final closure; only seal contact continuity has the supplied exception.
